claims.statement: The proposed paid unit is a monitored AI system or accepted evidence packet, while missed material changes and audit rework are the measurable losses; their monetary size is not evidenced.

Risk, compliance, security, legal, and model-governance teams are plausible budget owners because the AI Act assigns documentation, logging, quality, risk, and monitoring duties to relevant actors, but no buyer commitment exists.
The founder would need signed distribution and workflow agreements with trusted audit or GRC partners; no channel, vendor feed, or customer governance position is currently controlled.

The AI Act includes requirements around technical documentation, automatic logging, quality management, risk management, and post-market monitoring for covered systems and actors, supporting a recurring evidence problem without proving this product's demand.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Chief risk, compliance, model-risk, security, privacy, legal-operations, or AI-governance lead
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Stay vendor-neutral, preserve source-level provenance, map one delta across multiple control frameworks, and distribute through rather than displace trusted advisers
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Channel partner until the customer signs direct subscription and processing terms
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Audit, GRC, cyber, privacy, legal-operations, and managed-compliance channels

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Channel enablement, security review, proof of value, and enterprise sales; target recovery within the first annual contract
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Annual or quarterly subscription in advance; enterprise onboarding and security review may delay first cash
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Unvalidated target 65-80% after content, compute, reviewer, integration, support, and channel costs
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Automated collection and mapping with human review for materiality, ambiguity, disputes, and high-risk packets
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security program, professional liability, legal review, regulatory expertise, vendor terms, audit trail, and customer support
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Hypothesis: 600-2500 PLN per governed AI system per month, with enterprise minimums and separately priced historical evidence onboarding
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Source monitoring, licensed content, extraction and review, customer mappings, compute, alert QA, integrations, and partner share

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: GRC suites, model-governance platforms, audit firms, hyperscalers, and model vendors can add regulatory mappings and change notices
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Paid event is a monthly monitored-system subscription or accepted change-evidence packet; measurable loss is analyst rework, an unassessed material change, delayed approval, or an audit evidence gap
commercial_mechanics.payer: Regulated or high-consequence AI deployer, often through an audit, GRC, security, privacy, or managed-compliance partner
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: The organisation has several third-party AI systems, recurring vendor changes, and a named owner for documentation, logging, risk, or post-market evidence
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Annual platform renewal driven by ongoing model and vendor changes, audits, incidents, and control reviews

contrary_evidence: Many organisations may manage vendor evidence through existing GRC tickets, spreadsheets, procurement reviews, and annual audits.
Model vendors and hyperscalers may publish structured compliance portals that make third-party delta extraction unnecessary.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed 24-month nonexclusive distribution and workflow-integration agreement with defined lead ownership, data boundaries, service levels, and renewal economics
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Distribute directly to a narrow regulated niche, integrate another GRC partner, or sell fixed-scope evidence-delta reports without embedded workflow access
critical_control_point.current_owner: Audit, GRC, cyber, privacy, and legal-service firms; no founder distribution right is evidenced
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Channel partner until the customer signs direct subscription and processing terms
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed 24 months; no agreement is negotiated or signed
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: The founder has AI and analytical competence but no evidenced audit-firm distribution, vendor evidence feed, customer governance workflow, or regulatory authority.
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Each channel partner and each customer's authorised governance owner
critical_control_point.renewal: Annual renewal after the initial term based on activated systems, evidence acceptance, and low false-alert burden
critical_control_point.subject: Referral and workflow access to organisations with recurring third-party AI evidence obligations

economics.acquisition_route: Nonexclusive audit, GRC, cyber, privacy, and legal-operations partners serving a narrow regulated niche
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A high-retention evidence layer distributed through governance partners could scale across the EU; reaching 5m PLN likely requires hundreds of enterprise systems or strategic acquisition over 4-6 years
economics.founder_time: Up to five hours per day with bounded source coverage, automated diffs, and expert escalation only for ambiguous changes
economics.gross_margin_basis: Subscription less source licensing, collection, compute, expert review, integration, support, security, and channel share
economics.payback: Target recovery of partner onboarding and security review within the first annual contract; not evidenced
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 600-2500 PLN per governed AI system per month with enterprise minimums
economics.retention_or_repeat: Recurring while models, vendors, policies, incidents, and regulatory interpretations change

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A versioned map of vendors, model families, evidence objects, control impacts, reviewer decisions, and false alerts improves delta relevance
fingerprint.customer: Mid-market financial, health, employment, insurance, and public-service organisations deploying third-party AI systems
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Nonexclusive distribution through audit, cyber, privacy, legal-operations, GRC, and managed-compliance partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Curated vendor and regulatory change intelligence mapped to an organisation's evidence requirements, with requests, provenance, and exportable audit packets
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Risk, compliance, security, legal, or model-governance team pays a recurring fee per monitored AI system and accepted evidence packet
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A model version, vendor term, dataset statement, incident notice, intended use, or regulatory interpretation changes after initial approval

founder_fit: AI and data-science background supports model inventories, evidence extraction, mappings, and alert precision
Recurring intelligence is automation-friendly and compatible with limited founder hours after channel setup
The initial product can be built within 100k PLN using public evidence and customer-authorized documents
B2B channel distribution avoids dependence on a public founder persona
risks: An incomplete or incorrect mapping can create false assurance
Vendor sites, documentation, and contractual portals can block automated collection
Long security reviews and enterprise sales can exceed runway
Large GRC and audit incumbents can bundle the capability

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: recurring per system feed of source provenanced ai evidence changes
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: embedded channel position inside recurring audit grc cyber privacy and legal workflows
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: named governance owners enforcing continuous evidence change control across third party ai systems

structure.control_point: distribution inside audit and compliance workflows where evidence gaps become remediation work
structure.critical_dependency: customers adopting a repeatable change-control requirement rather than treating compliance as a one-time file

thesis: Future operating state (2029): regulated and high-consequence organisations treat every material AI model, data, policy, and vendor change as a controlled operational change. Missing contractual and data mechanism: a continuously maintained evidence feed that detects vendor deltas, maps them to each deployer's documented controls, requests missing attestations, and produces a signed change packet for the existing governance workflow.
title: AI Evidence Delta Feed
uncertainties: Which target organisations have recurring obligations, named owners, and enough third-party AI systems to pay
Whether vendor terms permit systematic monitoring and reuse of evidence
Alert precision and human review needed to avoid compliance fatigue
Exact boundary between evidence tooling, legal advice, conformity assessment, and regulated audit work
